newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Bad day seen ahead for Belgian shares.
newsitem.headline: Bad day seen ahead for Belgian shares.

text.p: The Bel-20 index, swooning on Thursday after an unexpected verbal blow by Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan, is likely to get an uppercut on Friday when news the U.S. might raise rates next week will have sunk in.
His comments knocked the Bel-20, already weakened by a combination of U.S. rate fears and worries in Europe EMU might be delayed, further down in the last 25 minutes of trade.
The index fell 2.54 percent, or 54.19 points, to 2,077.93 after recovering from a low of 2,069.59 in the dying seconds.
"It looks like tomorrow we'll see a lot of small sell orders," said Stefan Casteleyn at Corluy & Co.
In a testimony to U.S. Congress' Joint Economic Committee, Greenspan said that the economy retains "a great deal of vigor" and the jobs market is strong.
"Tonight it will be in the news and tomorrow people will probably sell," Casteleyn said.
He noted the Bel-20 was still six to seven percent higher compared with the start of the year and that retail investors might prefer to take profit.
"We could still shed these (six to seven percent)," he said.
Financial stocks were among those hit hardest with insurer Royale Belge hammered 5.2 percent.
Fellow insurer Fortis AG was 3.4 percent off.
All Bel-20 stocks ended in the red.
"The biggest losers are exactly those who had risen the most recently," Casteleyn said.
Cyclicals fared better with glass maker Glaverbel adding 1.4 percent to 4,075 francs and PVC profiles producer Deceuninck gaining 0.3 percent to 6,000.
Steel wire and cord maker Bekaert, which announced after the close that 1996 group net profit dipped to 2.28 billion francs from 3.01 billion, fell 3.3 percent to 20,800.
